summary: npm package used as hosting vehicle for a Cathay Pacific phishing landing page
details: The package ships a single file, index.html, which impersonates a Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' interstitial and embeds a Turnstile widget plus an obfuscator.io-obfuscated script containing hardcoded hostKey, aesKeyBase64, turnstileSiteKey, and a challengeLayoutHtml. The obfuscated code wires an onTurnstileComplete handler to window.__challengeRedirect, driving a client-side redirect after the Turnstile challenge completes. The package name (ticketcathayoct12) and content are consistent with a Cathay Pacific-themed phishing campaign, and the package appears to serve as a hosting vehicle so the HTML can be fetched through an npm-backed CDN. There are no lifecycle scripts and package.json main points at the HTML file, so npm install and require() of this package do not execute the content on an installer's machine; the harm target is end-user browsers that load the file via a CDN URL, not developers who install the package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
